_meta.notes: Colorado statewide elected executives. Unlike the legislature, all four offices run their own pressroom and every record attributes cleanly to a single officeholder. This is the strongest tier in the Colorado pilot: 574 items published 2026-01-01 to 2026-07-25 across the four offices, all four archives reaching past 2025-01-01, and every one collectable with hardened httpx. No Playwright needed anywhere in Colorado.
_meta.stale_url_correction: The 2026-05-01 recon listed https://governor.colorado.gov/press-releases. That host now fails the TLS handshake outright (LibreSSL SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL; DNS still resolves to 96.43.154.16). The live pressroom moved to https://www.colorado.gov/governor/news. Do not seed the old host.

pagination.note: Verified full back-walk: 89 pages, 890 distinct items, terminating cleanly when a page yields no new links.

scrape_config.date_note: No <time> element on the listing. Each card carries a 'Month D, YYYY' string; regex it and hand to parse_date_text(). 890 of 890 items dated this way in the 2026-07-25 verification run. Deduplicate on detail URL — the same article can render in more than one <article> block on a page.
scrape_config.rss_note: https://www.colorado.gov/governor/rss.xml returns 200 but is a 748-byte stub, not a usable item feed. Do not seed it.

members.notes: Highest-volume Colorado source of any tier — roughly 1.7 items per day in 2026. Mixes press releases, appointments, disaster declarations and 'What people are saying' roundups; all are first-party office output. Executive orders live on a separate page not seeded here.

pagination.note: WordPress, wp-json open and unauthenticated. Verified 1,097 posts back to 2019.

members.notes: Cleanest source in the whole Colorado pilot. Note /press-releases/ 301-redirects to /media-center/press-room/; seed the destination. Detail URLs still live under /press-releases/{slug}/.

pagination.note: The HTML index lists the current year only — 78 items, all 2026, as of 2026-07-25. Directory listings are 403 and there are no per-year index pages. The full archive is reachable from https://www.coloradosos.gov/sitemap.xml, which carries 1,609 press-release URLs back to 2004.

scrape_config.date_note: The date is encoded in the filename as PR{YYYYMMDD}. Exact, no parsing ambiguity, date_confidence 1.0. Listing link text also opens with 'Month D - '.

members.notes: Static HTML, deepest archive in the pilot. Volume tracks the election cycle — even years run two to three times odd years. Heavy candidate-qualification and ballot-certification output in 2026.

pagination.note: Drupal pager (ul.pagination.js-pager__items). Six pages, 51 distinct releases total.

scrape_config.date_note: The listing cards carry NO date — a listing-only parse yields 0 of 30 dated, verified 2026-07-25. The detail page has <time datetime="2026-06-11T09:00:00-06:00">, which is authoritative. This source requires a detail fetch per item. Volume is low enough (51 lifetime) that the cost is trivial.

members.notes: Lowest volume of the four — roughly two per month. /news and /press-releases both 404; the working path is /category/press-release. The 2026-05-01 recon flagged a 403 on direct fetch; that did not reproduce on 2026-07-25 with browser-class headers.
